families.note: All four read the letters of a word or phrase and compare them.

exercises.label: Isogram
exercises.idea: No letter may appear more than once, ignoring spaces and hyphens.
exercises.detail: It takes a word or phrase and returns true or false.

exercises.label: Pangram
exercises.idea: Every letter of the alphabet must appear at least once.
exercises.detail: It takes a sentence and returns true or false.

exercises.label: Anagram
exercises.idea: It keeps the candidates made of exactly the target's letters, but never the target itself.
exercises.detail: It takes a word and a list of words, and returns a list.

exercises.label: Acronym
exercises.idea: It joins the first letter of every word, in capitals.
exercises.detail: It takes a phrase and returns a short string of capitals.

families.note: All four do arithmetic on whole integers: their digits, divisors, or steps.

exercises.label: Armstrong numbers
exercises.idea: Its digits, each raised to the power of the digit count, add up to the value itself.
exercises.detail: It takes an integer and returns true or false.

exercises.label: Perfect numbers
exercises.idea: It compares an integer with the sum of its divisors below it.
exercises.detail: It takes an integer and returns one of three classes, or an error.

exercises.label: Collatz conjecture
exercises.idea: It halves an even value and triples an odd one plus one, counting steps until it reaches one.
exercises.detail: It takes an integer and returns a count of steps, or an error.

exercises.label: Leap
exercises.idea: Divisible by four, except centuries that are not divisible by four hundred.
exercises.detail: It takes a year and returns true or false.

families.note: All four turn letters into other letters by a rule, and most can undo it.

exercises.label: Atbash cipher
exercises.idea: It swaps each letter for its mirror in the alphabet, a for z, and groups the output in fives.
exercises.detail: It takes text and returns the encoded text.

exercises.label: Rotational cipher
exercises.idea: It shifts each letter a fixed number of places along the alphabet, wrapping around.
exercises.detail: It takes text and a shift, and returns the shifted text.

exercises.label: Affine cipher
exercises.idea: It maps each letter's index i to (a·i + b) mod 26, with a coprime to 26.
exercises.detail: It takes text and two keys, and returns encoded or decoded text.

exercises.label: Rail fence cipher
exercises.idea: It writes the message in a zigzag over several rows, then reads the rows off one after another.
exercises.detail: It takes text and a number of rows.

families.note: All four read or build a grid of rows and columns.

exercises.label: Minesweeper
exercises.idea: It counts, for every empty cell, the mines in the eight cells around it.
exercises.detail: It takes the rows of a board and returns the annotated rows.

exercises.label: Saddle points
exercises.idea: It finds the cells that are the largest in their row and the smallest in their column.
exercises.detail: It takes a grid of integers and returns positions.

exercises.label: Matrix
exercises.idea: It parses rows of integers out of a string and hands back one row or one column.
exercises.detail: It takes a string of lines and an index.

exercises.label: Word search
exercises.idea: It finds where each given term starts and ends in a grid, in any of eight directions.
exercises.detail: It takes a grid of letters and a list of terms, and returns positions.

families.note: All four answer with fixed English sentences built from their input.

exercises.label: Bob
exercises.idea: It answers a remark differently for a question, a shout, silence, or anything else.
exercises.detail: It takes a remark and returns one of five replies.

exercises.label: Raindrops
exercises.idea: It turns an integer into sounds by which of three, five, and seven divide it.
exercises.detail: It takes an integer and returns a string.

exercises.label: Two-fer
exercises.idea: It hands out one for a named person, or for you when there is no name, and one for me.
exercises.detail: It takes an optional name and returns a sentence.

exercises.label: Proverb
exercises.idea: It chains lines saying that for want of one thing, the next was lost.
exercises.detail: It takes a list of things and returns lines of text.

families.note: All four compute one integer from a count or a limit.

exercises.label: Sum of multiples
exercises.idea: It adds every integer below a limit that one of the given factors divides, counting each once.
exercises.detail: It takes a limit and a list of factors, and returns a total.

exercises.label: Difference of squares
exercises.idea: For the first n integers, it takes the square of their sum minus the sum of each one squared.
exercises.detail: It takes a count and returns an integer.

exercises.label: Nth prime
exercises.idea: It finds the n-th integer greater than one that only one and itself divide.
exercises.detail: It takes a position and returns an integer, or an error.

exercises.label: Grains
exercises.idea: It doubles a count on each of the 64 cells of a chessboard, and can total them.
exercises.detail: It takes a cell number and returns a count, or an error.

templates.title: Which exercise?
templates.description: A reference solution to an Exercism practice exercise, every name hidden: pick the exercise it solves.
templates.prompt: Which exercise does this code solve?
templates.evidence: This is {path} in {repository}, the track's reference solution to {name}.
templates.explanation: The answer is the exercise whose directory holds this solution; the other three come from the same family of exercises.
